Communication between home and school is continuous, with the Headteacher and staff at the gate a.m and p.m. Any matters raised at the gate are followed up systematically with phone calls and, if needed, action. Planners and Reading Diaries ensure ongoing dialogue.
The school provides a wealth of information on the children’s progress, targets and attainment. Curriculum Maps, annual curriculum meetings, an open door, weekly booster classes, holiday activities in English and Maths are all in place.
Parents are very happy with the induction and transition processes, and the full support they receive at these key points in their children’s lives. Welcome from the Headteacher
Thank you for your interest in Brookside Primary School. We are a community school which inspires each pupil to ‘strive for excellence everyday’. Here at Brookside, excellence means something different for everyone, as our pupils are encouraged to grow and develop at their own pace. We have a very rich school culture based on our diverse and inclusive school environment. We prioritise the holistic development of each child as we work in partnership with a range of stakeholders to provide the best learning opportunities both in and outside the classroom.
With a strong focus on building relationships, our teachers know our pupils very well. This has laid a strong foundation of behaviour for learning to drive our ambitious curriculum. We aim to create not just academically successful pupils but also learners who are aware of the ever-changing world around them, as they challenge themselves to discover what they are good at. Consequently, our pupils engage in a wide range of educational trips, sports activities, curriculum specific workshops, productions, projects and research, to build their confidence, promote British values, as well as enrich their lives. I am ambitious for all learners attending Brookside, and as such we will continue to set high expectations.
We hope that you will work with us and make Brookside the school of choice for your child. We look forward to a successful partnership between yourself, your child and our school.
Tishauna McMaster-Isaacs
Brooksideprimary@trhat.org
Perth Avenue, Hayes, Middlesex, UB4 9LW

About Us
Brookside Primary School has established itself as one of the best primary schools in the area, with pupils consistently achieving well above local and national standards in Early Years, Key Stage One and Key Stage Two. Its latest Ofsted report from March 2019 confirms that.
“High-quality teaching means that pupils make strong progress during key stage 2, particularly in writing and mathematics.” Brookside Primary is part of the family of schools sponsored by The Rosedale Hewens Academy Trust. The Trust has a proven track record of success and is responsible for a dramatic upturn in academic achievement locally.
Through its proven track record of success, the Academy Trust is able to work alongside Brookside to enhance and sustain the commitment to further drive up standards of academic achievement, attendance and behaviour.
The Rosedale Hewens Academy Trust is responsible for a number of primary schools and secondary colleges and therefore has the infrastructure, capacity and resources to make big improvements for children across both phases. Based on experience and driven by the priority to preserve small educational settings, the Trust is keen to maintain and promote schools where children are able to thrive because they are each known as individuals. This is achieved through formal structures of collaboration where groups of experienced practitioners work together to make positive change for those families which make up our local community. Through a common sense of purpose, educational vision and ethos, there is real scope for the Trust to further develop high quality local provision whilst at the same time allowing the school to retain its own distinctive character.
Brookside is able to benefit from the additional experience brought to the school by colleagues elsewhere in the wider Trust; able practitioners who are also passionate about making a real difference to the lives of children in our care. Working collaboratively as active partners, this enlarged group of professionals delivers a truly unique offer which benefits all stakeholders.
At Brookside Primary we aim to nurture happy, thoughtful children who grow up to make a difference in the world in which they live.
We provide an atmosphere which enables our children to acquire a wide range of knowledge, skills and practical abilities. We strive for excellence in all we do. Our school ethos is built around the 6 R’s of:
These R’s are used as a cornerstone in how we deal with all situations at our school and how we reward our children. We believe that by demonstrating the R’s every day, children will become positive members of their school and local community.
At Brookside, we are committed to providing high quality education for all of our learners, ensuring that every member of the school community is valued and respected, always being treated in a manner that is appropriate and just. We therefore aim to be a caring community where everyone is safe and secure. Good behaviour is a necessary condition before effective learning can take place. With that said, this does not mean a rigid or punitive system designed to enforce a particular set of rules. At Brookside, our priority is to promote positive relationships so that everyone can work productively together, sharing a common sense of purpose; each achieving the very best they can. Brookside rewards good behaviour, recognises success and regularly celebrates children’s achievement. We use praise to encourage good behaviour with the firm conviction that every child can become self-aware, independent and confident, both academically and socially.
At Brookside Primary, we wish to promote positive attitudes in the children and amongst all other stakeholders. With this in mind, we seek to fulfil our commitment to you, unimpeded by expectations that would otherwise limit the progress of your child at school.

The Academy Trust will only appoint additional teachers who will care deeply about the needs of the children in their care, knowing how to make learning effective and enjoyable.
Through an on-going programme of professional development, we can ensure that our teachers have a broad range of effective teaching strategies together with the ability to cultivate individual talents through a programme of personalised learning for each child. Through inspiring teaching, we aim to give each child a sense of well-being, encouraging courtesy and respect so that everyone can flourish and realise their full potential.
Working together, we will plan the educational journey of every child, drawing on the wider resources of the Academy Trust to ensure that there is both challenge and support. In many instances, teachers are encouraged to operate at the very forefront of local and national innovation, always combining this with tried and tested traditional teaching methods, backed up with approaches that make productive use of emerging technology.
In short, Brookside Primary School strives to achieve excellence, seeking to be among the highest performing schools in the Borough and beyond.

Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA)
We are delighted to announce that Brookside Primary School has been awarded the Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA) status.
Brooside Primary has been recognised for effective parental engagement leading to a substantial improvement in pupils’ learning and development. We aim to maintain a partnership with all parents, guardians and carers to ensure improved outcomes in all aspects of school life. We will continue to build on current good practice as well as nurture new initiatives to help us develop a culture of sincerity, mutual respect and support with families.
It is our genuine belief that the involvement of parents, guardians and carers in school life is pivotal to our continuous improvement and raising standards and achievement.
To read the full report, please click on the file below.

Family Support Hub – Best Start in Life
Best Start in Life is the UK Government’s central online hub designed to support parents and carers from pregnancy through to a child starting school. The site brings together trusted guidance, tools, and childcare information in one easy‑to‑navigate place. It provides personalised advice across every stage of early childhood, including pregnancy, baby care, toddler development, and school readiness.
The website also connects families with local Best Start Family Hubs, which act as single access points for parenting support, childcare information, health services, and community resources. Parents, guardians and carers can sign up for personalised weekly emails tailored to their child’s age or stage of pregnancy, offering helpful tips, activities, and development insights. Overall, Best Start in Life serves as a comprehensive, reliable resource to help families feel informed, supported, and confident during their child’s early years.
Brooksideprimary@trhat.org
Perth Avenue, Hayes, Middlesex, UB4 9LW

Childcare Funding Checker
The Best Start in Life Childcare Support Checker is designed to help families understand what financial support they may be entitled to. By entering a few details about your household, work situation, and children's ages, you can quickly see which childcare schemes you qualify for and how much you could save.
Parents can explore a full range of government-backed childcare offers, including 30 hours childcare for eligible working families, 15 hours early learning, Tax-Free Childcare, Universal Credit Childcare, and support for families where parents are studying.
In addition to financial support, the platform provides information on free breakfast clubs, wraparound childcare, and a wide selection of early years education options to help families plan the best childcare arrangement for their needs.
Whether you're looking for help with baby and toddler care, preparing your child for school, or understanding your childcare entitlements, the Best Start in Life hub brings all this information together in one place—making it easier for families to access the right support at the right time.

Brookside Primary School Open Days
Discover a School Where Every Child is Known, Valued and Inspired to Succeed
Choosing the right primary school is one of the most important decisions you'll make for your child. At Brookside Primary School, we believe every child deserves an outstanding start in life through exceptional teaching, high aspirations, and a nurturing environment where they can thrive.
Visit Our Open Days
There's no better way to see if Brookside is right for your family than by visiting us in person. Meet our staff, tour our facilities, explore our classrooms and discover the opportunities available to your child.
Thursday 17th September 2026 at 9:30am Tuesday 10th November 2026 at 10am
Wednesday 21st October 2026 at 4:00pm Tuesday 12th January 2027 4:00pm
Guided Tours – Every Friday at 11am
Join us at one of our Open Days and experience first-hand why so many local families choose Brookside.
Why Choose Brookside Primary School?
Ofsted Report
At Brookside, we are committed to helping every child reach their full potential academically, socially, and personally.
Our recent Ofsted report highlighted the strengths that make Brookside special:
"This is a happy and inclusive school, where everyone is known and valued."
"Pupils are kept safe at school."
"The school works hard to understand the needs of its pupils and ensure that these are catered for well."
"The school has constructed a curriculum which is well considered and carefully arranged."
High Achievement, High Expectations
We believe every child can achieve great things. Through excellent teaching, personalised support and ambitious learning opportunities, more Brookside pupils achieve Key Stage 2 scaled scores of 110+ than the national average.
A Caring and Inclusive Community
Brookside is more than a school - it's a community. Every child is supported, encouraged and celebrated throughout their educational journey. Our inclusive approach ensures children feel safe, confident and ready to learn every day.
We Are Closer Than You Think!
Conveniently located in Hayes, Brookside Primary School is easily accessible for local families across the area.

Back Into School: Resources for Families
The Children’s Commissioner provides a wide range of helpful resources to support families as children return to school. These include guidance on school attendance, how to apply for school places, and how to check eligibility for free school meals. Families can also access support for children moving from primary to secondary school through activity packs, as well as advice on mental health, including NHS guidance, BBC Bitesize wellbeing tips, and support from Young Minds. There are also dedicated resources to help parents understand and respond to bullying, alongside links to further support services.

Working Together to Support School Attendance
Members of the Attendance Action Alliance, in partnership with the Department for Education, have developed a short, practical guide to help parents, guardians and carers understand how they can work closely with their child’s school and local authority to support regular school attendance. This guide explains why being in school every day is so important for children’s learning, wellbeing, and development, and outlines the shared responsibilities families and schools have in helping children attend consistently.
Parents, guardians and carers can learn what to do if their child needs to be absent, what support is available when attendance becomes difficult, and how schools and local councils work together with families to remove barriers to attendance. The guide also provides clear information on the help available for children with long‑term illness, special educational needs, disabilities, or challenges at home or in school that make attending school harder.
It highlights who parents can speak to, how action plans are agreed, what adjustments schools can make, and the steps to take if further help is needed. By working in partnership, families, schools, and local authorities can ensure children receive the support they need to feel safe, confident, and able to attend school regularly.

Little Marvels Nursery Provision
Little Marvels provides exciting learning experiences for all its children where learning and play work in unison. Little Marvels is the perfect space for your child to learn, play and grow, as they fulfil their full potential in every aspect of personal development within the Early Years Framework. We provide high quality childcare whilst providing enriching experiences and enhanced learning opportunities.
We are a term time only nursery for children aged 2 to 4 years old, and operate between the hours of 8:00am to 4:00pm. We also support wrap-a-round care with Brookside Primary, providing the perfect opportunity for nursery school children to access both provisions and partake in various play experiences that will best support their development. We accept Government funding for 2 to 3-year-olds, and work closely with Brookside Primary School in order to deliver a smooth transition into school reception.
Spaces are currently available at our site situated in Brookside Primary School and our dedicated, highly qualified members of staff are ready to welcome you and your child into the nursery world! Please contact us on 07984075102 or click the button below to visit the website.
CONTACT LITTLE MARVELS
Business Services Manager: Lisa Kearne Telephone: 07984075102 Email Address: lkearne@trhat.org

Wraparound Care – Breakfast and After-School Clubs (7:45am to 6:00pm)
Our Wraparound Care Programme is designed with busy families in mind, this service provides a safe, structured, and inspiring environment where children can enjoy a wide range of enriching activities after the school day ends. From creative arts and dance to sports and skill-building sessions, our programme is carefully planned to support learning, confidence, and social development in a fun and inclusive setting. With flexible pick-up times and affordable pricing, we aim to make after-school care stress-free for parents while giving children opportunities to explore new interests, build friendships, and develop essential life skills. This is a chance for your child to experience afternoons filled with creativity, movement, and discovery—all while you manage your work commitments with peace of mind.
Why Choose Our Wraparound Care?
Pick Up Times & Prices
Our new pricing structure is designed to offer flexibility and value for families. Our care package offers your first session completely FREE when you book extended hours from 4:00pm to 6:00pm, giving you exceptional value. Whether you need care until 4:00pm for just £2, or extended hours until 5:00pm or 6:00pm, we’ve got you covered. This means an afternoon of care and activities costs just £4.50 until 5:00pm or £7.50 until 6:00pm, and the second or third session option includes a nutritious snack box plus enriching experiences your child will love. Affordable, convenient, and packed with benefits—our wraparound care is tailored to fit your family’s schedule and budget.
Funding Eligibility Checker
The Best Start in Life Eligibility Checker helps parents quickly find out if they qualify for funding, including support for free breakfast clubs and after‑school childcare. Just enter a few details to see which schemes you’re eligible for and how much you could save.
Our Breakfast Club runs every weekday morning from 7:45am to 8:30am, providing a safe and welcoming environment for children before the school day begins. We offer a nutritious breakfast, including options such as cereal, toast, fruit, and drinks, to help start the day right. The club is supervised by experienced staff and includes quiet activities to prepare children for learning. The cost is £1 per session, and places can be booked via iPayimpact. We look forward to seeing your child join us for a positive start to their day!
These sessions support families by offering opportunities for homework completion, creative activities, and skill-building in sports, arts, and mindfulness. Each club is tailored to promote personal growth—whether it’s boosting confidence through dance, developing teamwork in sports, or encouraging relaxation and reflection after a busy day.
3:15pm to 5:00pm (Includes Nutritional Snack Box)
3:15pm to 6:00pm (Includes Nutritional Snack Box)
Pick-up window: 3:15pm to 6:00pm (Arrive 5 minutes before your session ends to avoid late fees.)
Weekly Timetable and Details
Our Wraparound Clubs are designed to inspire, energize, and enrich every child’s afternoon. From the creativity of Dance, where children explore global rhythms and self-expression, to the fast-paced excitement of Basketball and Football, teamwork and fitness are at the heart of every session. For those who love precision and focus, Tennis and Golf offer skill-building in a calm, supportive environment. Each club is tailored to nurture confidence, cooperation, and a love for learning through play—ensuring your child enjoys every moment after school.
Please note: Our clubs will operate on a termly rotation to keep activities fresh, varied, and exciting for all children. As part of this schedule, Cricket and Rugby will be introduced during the second half of the Spring Term (after the February half-term break). This approach ensures every child has the opportunity to experience a wide range of sports and skills throughout the year.
Reading, Meditation and Reflection
Information About The Clubs
Homework & Crafting - Every Day
This session is designed to support parents by giving children dedicated time to complete homework in a calm, structured environment with guidance available if needed. We understand evenings can be busy, so this club helps reduce the pressure at home while ensuring homework is completed to a good standard. After finishing their tasks, children can enjoy creative crafting activities—encouraging imagination, fine motor skills, and relaxation. It’s the perfect balance of productivity and creativity, helping children stay on top of schoolwork while having fun in a supportive setting.
Monday - Golf
Golf Club introduces children to the basics of golf, focusing on technique, concentration, and patience. Using age-appropriate equipment, children will learn putting and swinging skills in a calm and enjoyable environment. This club is perfect for those who enjoy precision-based activities.
Tuesday - Multi-Sports Athletics
Our Multi‑Sports Athletics Club is a fun, active after‑school club designed to help children build confidence, coordination, and a love of sport. Sessions introduce pupils to a range of athletics‑based activities, including running, jumping, throwing, relay games, and team challenges.
Children will develop key physical skills such as speed, agility, balance, and stamina, while learning the importance of teamwork, perseverance, and fair play. Activities are adapted to suit all abilities, ensuring every child feels supported, included, and encouraged to try their best.
Wednesday - Tennis
Tennis Club introduces children to the fundamentals of the game, including grip, stance, and stroke techniques. Whether they are beginners or looking to improve, sessions are tailored to individual abilities. The club emphasizes patience, precision, and fun, helping children develop confidence on the court.
Thursday - Football
Football Club provides an exciting opportunity for children to develop ball control, passing, and tactical awareness. Through drills and mini-games, they’ll learn the importance of teamwork and fair play. Sessions are energetic and inclusive, ensuring every child feels part of the team.
Friday - Cricket
Cricket offers children the chance to learn and enjoy the fundamentals of cricket in a fun, supportive after‑school environment. Pupils will develop core skills such as batting, bowling, fielding, and catching through engaging drills, games, and small‑sided matches. The club focuses on building confidence, coordination, teamwork, and sportsmanship while encouraging all abilities to take part and progress at their own pace. With an emphasis on enjoyment, fair play, and active participation, Cricket is a great way for children to stay active, try a traditional team sport, and grow their love of the game.
Arts and Crafts, Board Games and Meditation Time - Every Day
Our Arts and Crafts, Board Games and Meditation Time wraparound club offers a calm, creative and enjoyable end to the school day. Children can express their creativity through a range of arts and crafts activities, challenge themselves and socialise with friends through classic board games, and unwind during guided meditation time designed to promote relaxation and wellbeing. This balanced session provides a nurturing environment where children can have fun, build friendships and develop important social and emotional skills before heading home.
Important Information
Snack Box - What's Included
The below will be given to your child between 4:00pm and 4:15pm if you have booked a second or third session. Once your booking is confirmed via iPayimpact, you will receive a form to select the options you would like your child to enjoy.
Each box includes a balanced mix of carbs, protein, fruit, and veg:
1. Mini Sandwich (Wholemeal bread with a healthy filling such as): - Tuna - Chicken - Cheese - Tomato and cucumber - Honey
2. Fresh Fruit Portion (Apple slices, satsuma or banana) or Vegetable Sticks (Cucumber or carrots)
4. Drink (Milk or Water)
PE Kit
If your child is booked for a second session that involves physical activities (such as sports or dance), please ensure they bring their PE kit to school. Children will change into their kit during the Homework & Crafting session before their activity begins. This helps them be ready and comfortable for their chosen club.
